modules.title: Responsible AI principles
modules.summary: Six principles guide any AI solution at Microsoft. The exam asks you to recognize which one applies in a specific situation.
points: Fairness: the system treats all people comparably; bias in data and outcomes is monitored.
Reliability and safety: it behaves as expected, even with unexpected inputs, and is tested before release.
Privacy and security: it protects personal data and resists attacks.
Inclusiveness: it serves people with different abilities, languages and contexts.
Transparency: people know they are dealing with AI, how it works and what its limits are.
Accountability: there are people who answer for the system and can oversee or correct it.

modules.title: Generative AI models: how they work and how they are configured
modules.summary: A generative model predicts the next token from the context. Choosing the right model, deployment type and parameters decides cost, latency and quality.
points: Text is split into tokens; the model turns them into vectors (embeddings) and uses attention to decide which parts of the context weigh more.
The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model considers across instructions, history and response.
Temperature and top-p control how varied the response is; the maximum output tokens limits its length.
To answer with your own, recent data you use grounding (RAG); fine-tuning changes the model's behavior and costs more.
Small language models (SLMs) are cheaper and faster; large and multimodal ones cover more complex tasks or tasks with image and audio.
Standard deployment is billed per token consumed; provisioned deployment reserves capacity for predictable latency.

modules.title: AI workloads: text, speech, vision and extraction
modules.summary: The exam describes a scenario and asks you to identify the right workload and technique.
points: Text analysis: key phrase extraction, entity detection, sentiment analysis and summarization.
Speech: recognition (speech to text) and synthesis (text to speech).
Vision: classifying an image, detecting objects and their location, reading text (OCR) or describing the image; generation models create new images from text.
Information extraction: turning documents, images, audio and video into structured fields.
Generative AI creates content; agentic AI also uses tools and takes steps to reach a goal.

modules.title: Generative AI apps and agents with Foundry
modules.summary: From prompt to agent: deploying a model in a Foundry project, testing it in the playground, calling it from code and giving it instructions and tools.
points: The system message sets role, tone, limits and format; the user message carries the specific request.
A good prompt gives context, clear instructions, examples and the expected output format.
In the Foundry portal you choose a model from the catalog, deploy it in a project and test it in the playground.
A client app uses the project endpoint and the deployment name; it keeps the message history to preserve context.
An agent combines a model, instructions and tools (for example, file search or code execution) and keeps the conversation in a thread.

modules.title: Text and speech solutions with Foundry
modules.summary: Analyzing text and conversing by voice, either with a deployed multimodal model or with Azure Speech in Foundry Tools.
points: A generative model can do text analysis with a prompt: summarizing, classifying sentiment or extracting entities.
Multimodal models accept audio as input and can respond to a spoken prompt.
Azure Speech in Foundry Tools offers speech to text and text to speech, with neural voices in many languages.
For a voice app: capture the audio, transcribe it, generate the response and synthesize it.

modules.title: Vision and generated images with Foundry
modules.summary: Interpreting images inside a prompt with a multimodal model and creating new images with a generative model.
points: A multimodal model receives text and image in the same prompt and can describe, compare or answer questions about the image.
An image generation model creates an image from a text description; the detail of the prompt defines the result.
In an app, the image is sent as a URL or as encoded data together with the message text.
Content filters apply both to prompts and to generated images.

modules.title: Information extraction with Content Understanding
modules.summary: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools turns documents, images, audio and video into structured data through analyzers.
points: An analyzer defines which content to process and which fields to return; there are prebuilt and custom analyzers.
In a custom analyzer you describe a field schema (name, type and description) and the service extracts the fields.
From documents and forms you get fields such as dates, totals or names; from images, descriptions and attributes.
From audio and video you get transcripts, summaries and fields per segment.
The client app sends the file to the analyzer and receives the result as JSON.

questions.q: A bank finds that its loan model rejects applicants from a certain postal code more often than others with the same history. Which principle is being breached?
questions.why: Treating people with the same profile differently is a fairness problem (bias in data or outcomes).

questions.q: Your team publishes a chatbot and adds a notice: "These answers are generated by AI and may contain errors". Which principle does that notice address?
questions.why: Transparency: people must know they are interacting with AI and know its limits.

questions.q: Before releasing a medical assistant, the team tests it with ambiguous and out-of-scope questions to verify it gives no dangerous instructions. Which principle applies?
questions.why: Reliability and safety: the system must behave safely with unexpected inputs too.

questions.q: A company appoints a person who reviews the AI system's decisions and can correct them or suspend it. Which principle does this describe?
questions.why: Accountability: there are people who answer for the system and oversee it.

questions.q: A voice assistant misrecognizes people with regional accents and offers no text alternative. Which principle should be strengthened?
questions.why: Inclusiveness: the solution must serve people with different ways of speaking and different abilities.

questions.q: You need a model to answer with information from your company's internal manuals, which change every week. Which approach fits best?
questions.why: RAG brings the current documents into the prompt without retraining the model; weekly fine-tuning would be expensive and slow.

questions.q: A model gives different answers each time for a classification task that must be consistent. Which parameter do you adjust first?
questions.why: A low temperature reduces randomness and makes the output more repeatable.

questions.q: What are tokens in a language model?
options: The access keys to the service
The units of text (words or fragments) the model processes
The trained parameters of the model
questions.why: Text is split into tokens; consumption and the context limit are also measured in them.

questions.q: An app processes a high, steady volume of requests and needs predictable latency. Which deployment type fits?
options: A local model on each computer
Any; deployment does not affect latency
questions.why: Provisioned deployment reserves processing capacity and gives predictable performance for steady workloads.

questions.q: To classify short e-mails into three categories at the lowest cost and latency, which model do you choose?
questions.why: For simple, high-volume tasks, a small model costs less and responds faster.

questions.q: An insurer wants to automatically get the policy number, date and amount from thousands of scanned forms. Which workload is it?
questions.why: Turning documents into structured fields is information extraction.

questions.q: Marketing wants to know which topics come up most in 10,000 customer comments. Which technique do you use?
questions.why: Key phrase extraction identifies the main topics of each text.

questions.q: An app must read the news aloud to people with low vision. Which capability does it need?
questions.why: Converting text into audio is speech synthesis.

questions.q: A warehouse needs to know how many boxes are in each photo and where each one is. Which vision technique applies?
questions.why: Object detection identifies each object and its location; classification only labels the whole image.

questions.q: What distinguishes an agentic AI solution from a simple generative chat?
options: It can use tools and carry out steps to reach a goal
questions.why: An agent plans and acts with tools; a simple chat only generates a response.

questions.q: You want the assistant to always answer in English, in at most three bullets and without giving legal advice. Where do you put those rules?
questions.why: The system message defines role, tone, limits and format for the whole conversation.

questions.q: Your chat app forgets what the user said two messages ago. What is the most likely cause?
options: The app does not send the message history on each call
questions.why: The model keeps no memory between calls: the app must send the history to preserve context.

questions.q: In the Foundry portal you have already chosen a model from the catalog. What must you do before using it in the playground or from code?
questions.why: A catalog model is deployed in the project to get a deployment that requests are sent to.

questions.q: Which elements define an agent in Foundry?
options: An analyzer and a field schema
questions.why: An agent combines a deployed model, instructions that set its behavior and tools to act with.

questions.q: A model responds generically to "write an e-mail". What improves the result most?
options: Giving context, recipient, tone, an example and the expected format
questions.why: Effective prompts give context, specific instructions, examples and an output format.

questions.q: You need an app that turns recorded calls into text to analyze them later. Which Azure Speech capability do you use?
questions.why: Transcribing audio is speech recognition (speech to text).

questions.q: With a deployed generative model you want to classify reviews as positive, negative or neutral. What is the simplest way?
options: With a prompt that asks for the classification and defines the three labels
Raising the temperature to the maximum
questions.why: A generative model can do text analysis with a clear prompt that fixes the output categories.

questions.q: A user wants to talk to the app and get an answer without typing. Which type of model accepts audio directly as input?
questions.why: Multimodal models accept more than one type of input, including audio.

questions.q: A kiosk must give spoken directions in several languages with a natural voice. What do you need?
questions.why: Speech synthesis with neural voices produces natural audio in many languages.

questions.q: From a contract you want the signing parties, the dates and the amounts. Which text analysis technique is it?
questions.why: Entity detection identifies people, organizations, dates and quantities in the text.

questions.q: A user uploads a photo of a control panel and asks "which alarm is on?". What do you need?
options: A multimodal model that receives image and text in the same prompt
questions.why: To reason about an image together with a question you use a multimodal model.

questions.q: The design team wants new sketches from written descriptions. Which type of model do you use?
questions.why: Image generation models create new images from a text prompt.

questions.q: A generated image comes out different from what you expected. Which adjustment gives the most control over the result?
options: Describing the subject, style and composition in more detail in the prompt
questions.why: In image generation, the detail of the prompt is what defines the result most.

questions.q: In a client app, how is an image sent to a multimodal model?
options: As part of the message, together with the text, through a URL or the image data
By converting it to audio first
It cannot be done: they only accept text
questions.why: The message includes the text and the image (by URL or encoded) in the same request.

questions.q: What is the difference between interpreting an image and generating an image?
options: Interpreting takes an image and returns text; generating takes text and returns an image
questions.why: They are opposite directions: vision as input versus image as output.

questions.q: In Content Understanding, what defines which fields are extracted from a piece of content?
options: The analyzer and its field schema
questions.why: An analyzer declares the content type and the schema of fields to return.

questions.q: You want to get from invoices a field of your own, "cost center", that is not in the prebuilt analyzers. What do you do?
options: Use OCR and look for it by hand
Create a custom analyzer that includes that field in its schema
questions.why: A custom analyzer lets you describe your own fields so the service extracts them.

questions.q: From recordings of support calls you need the transcript and a summary per call. What do you use?
options: Content Understanding with an audio analyzer
questions.why: Content Understanding processes audio and returns the transcript and fields such as the summary.

questions.q: In which format does the client app receive an analyzer's result?
questions.why: The result arrives as JSON with the extracted fields, ready to use in the app.

questions.q: Which types of content can Content Understanding process?
questions.why: The service is multimodal: documents and forms, images, audio and video.
